transcript.text: Unplug it first and never remove the outer casing. “Not working” can mean anything from a switched-off socket or plug fuse, to the door not registering as shut, a control lock/settings issue, or an internal fault. First, check that the socket is switched on and that another appliance works in it; do not remove the microwave casing to inspect fuses. Then tell me whether its display is completely blank, or whether it powers up but will not start or does not heat a cup of water. That split will point us to the right next check.
display is on, shows the time. beeps when I press buttons but won't start

Because the display and buttons are alive, this is unlikely to be a socket or power-fuse problem. The most likely causes are that the door interlock is not detecting the door as properly shut, or a control/child lock is set; less commonly it is a keypad or control fault. Unplug it, then check that the door closes with a firm click and that the plastic hooks and the slots they enter are clean and undamaged—do not remove the casing. Also look for a lock/key symbol, or try the control-lock release shown on the panel (often holding Stop/Cancel for a few seconds). Does the door latch positively, and is any lock symbol showing?
door shuts fine I think. there's a little L symbol on the display. holding stop for a few secs?

Yes — that is the right first thing to try. The little “L” is very likely the control/child lock, which allows the display and beeps but prevents it starting. Hold Stop/Cancel for around 3–5 seconds (on some panels it can be nearer 5 seconds) until the L disappears, then set a time and press Start. If the L stays on, try holding the button marked with a lock/key symbol instead; if it unlocks but still will not start, the door interlock becomes the next most likely cause.
ok holding stop for 3 secs made the L go away and it works now. thanks
That was the control/child lock, not a fault. Is there anything else you need help with?
